title: Percentage Power — Mental % in 3 Seconds
subtopics: 10% anchor — any percentage as multiple of 10%
Commutative trick: x% of y = y% of x
Challenge — compound interest 2 years at 10% on ₹1000
learningGoals: Compute any percentage mentally using the 10% anchor and build-up
Apply the commutative trick (x% of y = y% of x) to simplify calculations
Calculate compound discounts and compound interest without a calculator
coreIdeas: 10% of any number = number ÷ 10 — all other percentages build from here
x% of y = y% of x — choose whichever direction is easier
Successive discounts compound: 20% then 10% = 28% total, not 30%

starterPractice.q: State the commutative trick for percentages.
starterPractice.a: x% of y = y% of x

starterPractice.q: Are two successive 10% discounts the same as one 20% discount?

onboarding.welcomeMessage: Every price tag, every exam mark, every sale — percentages are everywhere. Master them in 3 seconds!

duolingoLessonArc.mission: Compute any percentage mentally using the 10% anchor, commutative trick, build-up, and compound formulas.
microLessonPattern: Coach shows the anchor value (10% of the number)
Build the target percentage from anchors

reviewLoop.action: Show anchor value and rebuild the target step by step

sessionFlow.coachHook: 10% is just divide by 10. From there you can build ANY percentage!
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: '10% of 460 is 46. Double it for 20%. Halve it for 5%.'

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Flip It — x% of y = y% of x
sessionFlow.coachHook: 16% of 25 looks hard. But 25% of 16 = 16÷4 = 4. Same answer, way easier!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show 16% of 25 → flip → 25% of 16 = 4. Then 4% of 75 → 75% of 4 = 3.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'If one direction is ugly, flip — multiplication is commutative.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Compute 4% of 25 using the flip trick.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Always check: does flipping give a nicer percentage (25%, 50%, 10%)?

exercises.questionText: Compute 16% of 25 using the commutative trick (x% of y = y% of x).

sessionFlow.coachHook: Any percentage = sum of simpler ones. 37% = 30%+5%+2%. Build it brick by brick!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: 37% of 200: 30%=60, 5%=10, 2%=4. Total=74. Show on a bar segment diagram.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'Decompose 37% into 30, 5, and 2 percent. Add the three parts.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Compute 23% of 300 using the build-up method.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Choose decompositions that are multiples of 10%, 5%, or 1% for easy mental math.

exercises.questionText: Compute 37% of 200 using the build-up method (30%+5%+2%).

sessionFlow.coachHook: A shopkeeper gives 20% off, then 10% more off. You'd expect 30% total — but it's actually 28%!
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'Successive discounts multiply, not add. Always.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Find the total discount for 25% then 20% off.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Start with 100. After 25%: 75. After 20% of 75: 60. Discount=40.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Four options but only one correct percentage. Use your anchor and build-up skills to check.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Show a MCQ where wrong options correspond to common errors (e.g. adding instead of compounding).

sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Estimation is powerful: 37% of 200 ≈ 40% of 200 = 80 — so the answer is just under 80.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Compound interest means interest on interest! At 10% for 2 years on ₹1000 — compute it purely mentally.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Year 1: 1000+10%=1100. Year 2: 1100+10%=1210. CI=210. Simple interest would be 200. Extra=₹10.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Read aloud: 'Compound interest earns interest on the interest from year 1.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Compute compound interest at 10% for 2 years on ₹2000.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: CI for 2 years at r% on P = P[(1+r/100)²-1]. At 10%: P×0.21.

exercises.questionText: Compute compound interest on ₹1000 at 10% per year for 2 years.

exercises.questionText: On ₹1000 at 10% for 2 years, compound interest is ₹210 while simple interest is ₹200. What is the extra amount due to compounding?
exercises.solution: The extra ₹10 is 10% of ₹100 (the Year 1 interest), earned as interest-on-interest in Year 2.
